summary: In this excerpt from a fiction novel (Book 1, part 62), narrator Marcus, who goes by the handle M1k3y, feels responsible for the Xnet, a network that has begun monitoring people as statistically abnormal, and cannot stop it. He wishes he could consult Jolu, an ISP worker at Pigspleen Net, and the team meets at their favorite Mission cafe, officially for their Harajuku Fun Madness meeting, now canceled. The team is grieving Darryl's disappearance, and Vanessa (Van) argues with Marcus that his Xnet activity risks jail for himself and many others, while he insists he is acting for Darryl and for the country's rights.
one_line: Marcus and his friends argue at a Mission cafe about his risky Xnet activity after Darryl's disappearance and the canceled game.
key_facts: Jolu worked at an Internet Service Provider called Pigspleen Net that had hired him when he was twelve.
The narrator believes the Xnet, once running, had a life of its own and that he could not stop it.
The team meets at their favorite place in the Mission after school, officially for the weekly Harajuku Fun Madness team meeting.
The Harajuku Fun Madness game has been canceled and Darryl is gone, leaving the meetings mostly weekly weep-fests.
The team receives about six phone calls and IMs a day asking, "Are you OK? Did it really happen?"
Vanessa arrived in her girl's school uniform, a Sailor Moon-style pleated skirt, tunic and knee-socks.
Vanessa was stuck going the long way home, down to the San Mateo bridge and back, on a shuttle-bus service her school operated.
The cafe was full of older, cooler emo art students who snickered into their lattes when Vanessa arrived.
Vanessa calls the narrator M1k3y in the meeting and says he is putting himself at risk.
The narrator's handle M1k3y is now associated with his Xnet use, which scared him to hear said aloud in public.
Vanessa tells the narrator he could go to jail, and so could lots of people, after what happened to Darryl.
The narrator says, "I'm doing this for Darryl!" and lowers his voice after art students look at them.
Vanessa says the narrator is out of his mind because the government is the one that would stop them.
The narrator replies, "It's still our country," and says they still have the right to do this.
The narrator says the government puts people under the microscope just for being statistically abnormal.
